PR #131 · stack layer 08 / 2660 files +1,298 −544

The snapshot becomes the input.

Required policy sections reach 19 production files. The default definitions already exist; mechanisms remain in apps/cli. Returned-error and test-fixture changes are part of this delta too.

The decisions

Unexplained consequences first. Open a row only where you need the mechanism or evidence.

AreaDelta to hold in your headReason found
01Returned error After a reattachment is accepted, a failing completion now exposes that attempt’s error. Before, the first connection error survived both reattachment failure paths. UnexplainedThis consequence of the loop rewrite is absent from the PR’s stated decisions. +

Returned error · mechanism and evidence

The catch boundary moved. This is a source-level observation; no rationale for choosing the returned error was found.

Same sequenceBaseHead
Initial accepted connection fails with E₀; reattachment fails before acceptanceE₀E₀
Initial accepted connection fails with E₀; reattachment is accepted, then its completion rejects with E₁E₀E₁

At the default reattachment limit of one, the head’s next loop iteration catches E₁ and throws it. The base awaited the reattached completion inside the catch that rethrew E₀. This concerns rejected promises; a resolved {status: "failed"} completion follows the existing return path.

The local probe executes these two method bodies extracted from source, with stubbed completion promises. It does not start a daemon or exercise sockets.

Catch boundary in the diff Base method Head method

PR context and decisions Workspace composition Process composition Command composition Existing policy owner
05Response deadlines Composition purpose selects 100 ms for a status observer and 250 ms for ordinary lifecycle / execution-status exchanges. Execute admission stays 5 s; acceptance clears that timer. StatedPR: status observation and ordinary execution-status requests have distinct deadlines. +

Response deadlines · mechanism and evidence

The purpose is chosen when constructing the transport, not by testing the request’s kind. Status command composition passes responseTimeoutPurpose: "status-observer". Normal transports keep the ordinary purpose. The policy values existed before this PR; the selector replaces a numeric 100 ms option at that composition site.

Status chooses the purpose Constructor and acceptance Purpose characterization tests Recorded deadlines and reasons
06Recovery scopes Numeric counters replace fixed recovery control flow: 1 execution reattachment per call; 1 fetch-resume allowance inside each execute attempt. A failed fetch feeds completion failure; a reattachment gets a fresh allowance. StatedPR: each reattached execute attempt needs its own fetch-resume allowance. +

Recovery scopes · mechanism and evidence

BoundaryCondition / lifetime
Execution reattachmentclosed error, delivery already accepted, authenticated instance matches the request; counter belongs to completeWithReattachments.
Fetch resumeCounter belongs to executeOnce. Resume requires acceptance and a manifest, and no terminal / settled completion.
Failed fetchfetchCompletion(...).catch(fail) rejects that completion. It does not recursively call the resume function. The outer reattachment path can then apply.
Numeric generalityThe page illustrates the default limit of one. A numeric guard alone is not evidence of repeated fetch attempts for a value greater than one.

The base already had one reattachment and a resume boolean local to each executeOnce. The change makes those limits policy inputs. It does not introduce either recovery path or a shared boolean that formerly covered both.

Counters and their surrounding control flow Resume failure path Reattached-attempt fetch witness Stated recovery reason

Control caps stay 8 MiB JSON / 256 KiB execution control. StatedPR + policy record: require the slice throughout the bounded output path. +

Enforcement boundary · mechanism and evidence

BoundaryHead
Meta-testScans concatenated app production source text for a list of retired constants, optional threshold spellings, and local policy ownership names. It does not trace value flow.
Registry grace overridestartupOwnerIsWithinGrace(owner, graceMs = policy.coordinationGraceMs, now) retains an explicit optional numeric grace argument. Production call sites inspected here omit it. Unexplained: no reason found for retaining the override.
Transport write chunkwriteChunkSize?: number remains in the production transport options. It controls how encoded frames are split across socket writes. Unexplained: no reason found for retaining this seam.
Projected numeric argumentsCodec encode / decode, transfer decoder, file reader, and worker response validation require limits as arguments. Production callers project them from policy.
Package boundaryapps/cli → @symnav/daemon remains the import direction. No package dependency file changes in this PR; mechanisms stay app-owned.
User configurationThe existing no-user-tuning contract remains: no flag, environment variable, or config file for policy thresholds.

The named-string guard is evidence of its specific enforcement mechanism, not proof that every possible numeric bypass is impossible.
